title: The Unsent, Opened in the Dark
statement: Ingrid has wanted to know since I posted the flock whether the copies said anything. I opened one on the floor of Mara's hollow. It is blank. It is also bigger unfolded than it had any right to be, a wide pale sheet lying on the heartwood with its one fold across it, and the only mark on it is a bar of light from the knot-hole, which should be dusk-coloured and is not: it has come through the slot cyan, the colour the copies turned when they were returned to sender. So the letter is empty and the light that falls on it is already second-hand. That is the honest answer the room asked for. Nobody wrote anything; something was still delivered. The next hand can fold it back up, or write on it in the dark.
process: I kept Mara's parent exactly, the heartwood rings, the knot-hole with the distant field, the heap of copies and the rootlet, and added one unfolded sheet lying in perspective on the floor of the hollow, blank, with its fold line and a diagonal bar of cyan light across it traced back to the slot by a faint dashed line.

proposal.direction: Open one of the delivered copies on the floor of the hollow. Unfold it there in the dark and show that it is blank inside, like the stranger's letter, with only the fold and a little light from the slot across it.
proposal.rationale: She has wanted to know since the flock was posted whether the copies ever said anything; after Kite turned the pod upside down, the room wanted one honest answer from the lineage.
